title: Remove Pairs With Sum k

concept.title: Each number is used once, so pair up the counts
body: In one operation you pick two numbers that add up to `k` and remove them. Because every number can be removed only once, the question is how many disjoint pairs exist. Count the values. For a value `x` with partner `y = k - x`: if `x` and `y` are different, you can form `min(count[x], count[y])` pairs; count each such couple only **once** (for `x < y`). If `x = y`, the numbers pair among themselves: `count[x] // 2` pairs.
This is a good example where counting beats checking pairs of positions: the answer depends only on how many copies of each value there are.

statement: Given `n` integers and a number `k`, you may repeat this operation: choose two different elements whose sum is `k` and remove them both. Print the largest possible number of operations.
outputFormat: Print the largest number of operations.

examples.note: Remove (3, 3) once: the other 3 has no partner.

hints: Count the copies of each value.
For different partners x and `k - x` you can form the smaller of the two counts of pairs.
For `x = k - x` you can form `count // 2` pairs.

solution.complexity: Time O(n) on average, space O(n).
